prd.name: Debug Mock TTY
prd.overview: A debug-only mock TTY built into the Rust core (bedterm_core) and surfaced in the iOS app as an in-app entry point. In Debug builds the Hosts screen exposes a "Debug TTY" group with four launchable programs (echo shell, vim-lite, replay, raw sink) that drive the existing terminal pipeline end-to-end with no SSH. The same Rust mock provides a cargo-level loopback against alacritty_terminal, giving the VTE integration its first end-to-end regression coverage. Release builds contain none of this code or its symbols.
prd.why: Manual testing of terminal rendering, key-bar input, IME composition, alt-screen apps (vim-class), and modern TUIs (Claude Code, Codex) currently requires a live SSH session. That is slow to set up, depends on the network, and offers no determinism. At the same time, the Rust core's alacritty_terminal integration has no end-to-end test path — the bytes-in/grid-out loop is only exercised through the iOS UI. A single Rust-side mock solves both: Swift wraps it as an SSHClient for hands-on debugging on device or simulator, and Rust pipes it into Term for cargo test assertions on grid state. Building the mock in Rust (rather than Swift) is justified specifically by the cargo-test payoff; the iOS debug entry is a near-free byproduct.

requirement.name: Rust Mock TTY Core
requirement.description: A Rust module inside bedterm_core implements a pluggable mock TTY: a small termios state machine plus a Program trait whose implementations produce the output byte stream. The module is feature-gated; Release builds omit it entirely.
requirement.rule: The mock TTY module compiles only when the bedterm_core Cargo feature mock-tty is enabled. Release xcframework builds disable the feature; Debug builds enable it.
A Release-flavoured xcframework contains no bt_mock_tty_* exported symbols (verified by nm in CI).
The C FFI exposes exactly six symbols: create, free, set_output_callback, write, resize, tick. No other mock-related symbols are exported.

The termios state machine implements ICANON, ECHO, ECHOE, ISIG, ICRNL, ONLCR, and the control chars VINTR (0x03), VERASE (0x7F), VEOF (0x04). Programs may switch between cooked and raw mode at runtime.

Each Program implementation is self-contained: its only inputs are bytes, resize events, and tick events; its only output is bytes. Programs cannot reach into the FFI or the termios state of another program.
A debug-assertion-only guard inside the mock panics if a caller re-enters the handle from within the output callback. The Swift wrapper must not violate this rule.

requirement.name: Echo Shell Program
requirement.description: A cooked-mode interactive prompt with a small set of built-in commands targeted at terminal-renderer and keyboard-input verification.
requirement.rule: The shell prints "bedterm-debug$ " at start and after every command. Backspace, Ctrl-U, and CR behave per ICANON line discipline.

The "keys" command enters a sub-mode that prints each received input byte as a hex value with a mnemonic (e.g., 0x1B ESC) until the user presses q. Verifies KeyBar, soft-keyboard, IME, and arrow-key byte sequences.
The "colors" command emits a 16-colour bar, a 256-colour block, and a 24-bit truecolor gradient. Verifies SGR handling at each colour depth.
The "cursor" command emits CUP, CHA, and DECTCEM sequences that leave a known checkerboard pattern. Verifies cursor-positioning and show/hide rendering.
The "altscreen" command enters the alternate screen (ESC[?1049h), draws a banner, waits, and exits (ESC[?1049l). Verifies alt-screen save/restore in the renderer.
"demo vim", "demo codex", "demo claude" each switch to the replay program loaded with the corresponding bundled cast fixture, then return to the echo shell when the fixture finishes.
The "stress" command emits a stream of random cursor positioning plus truecolor SGR for several seconds. Manual Metal renderer stability check.
"vim" switches the active program to vim-lite. "clear" issues ESC[2J + cursor home. "exit" closes the session.

requirement.name: Vim-Lite Program
requirement.description: A minimal modal editor used to exercise alt-screen flow, mode-driven key handling, and resize behaviour against the renderer.
requirement.rule: On entry the editor enters the alternate screen, hides the cursor briefly, draws a seeded buffer plus a status line, and sets cursor shape to block (ESC[2 q). On exit it restores the previous screen and resets cursor shape.

In NORMAL mode the keys h, j, k, l move the cursor; 0 and $ jump to line start/end; gg and G jump to file start/end; x deletes a character; dd deletes a line; i, a, o enter INSERT mode; : enters COMMAND mode.
In INSERT mode the cursor shape is bar (ESC[6 q). Printable bytes append at the cursor. 0x7F deletes the character to the left. 0x1B (ESC) returns to NORMAL mode.
In COMMAND mode the user types after ':' on the status line. ":q" exits to the echo shell, ":w" flashes "written" on the status line, ":wq" does both. ESC aborts the command.
A resize event triggers a full redraw of the buffer and status line at the new dimensions.

requirement.name: Replay Program
requirement.description: Plays back a recorded asciinema v2 cast file at its recorded timing, so the renderer can be exercised against authentic vim, Codex, and Claude Code byte streams without depending on a live session.
requirement.rule: The replay program accepts asciinema v2 cast files (JSONL: one header object plus rows of [time, "o", bytes]). Non-output rows are skipped. No external JSON dependency is used.

A wall-clock tick driven from Swift releases all events whose recorded time is less than or equal to elapsed wall time since the program started. Tick frequency is not normatively specified but must be fine enough for visually smooth replay (60 Hz suffices).

Three cast files ship with the Debug build: a vim editing session, a Codex TUI session, and a Claude Code session. The Codex and Claude Code fixtures must exercise synchronized output (ESC[?2026), bracketed paste, truecolor, and OSC 8 hyperlinks where present.
Each bundled cast file has a sibling README entry describing what was recorded, when, with which app version, so it can be re-recorded as those apps evolve.

requirement.name: Raw Sink Program
requirement.description: A pass-through program that produces no shell behaviour, used to inspect exactly which bytes the iOS input surfaces produce for each key, gesture, and IME interaction.
requirement.rule: Every input byte is delivered to output unchanged. Termios runs in raw mode (no ICANON, no ECHO, no ICRNL, no ONLCR).
The raw sink program does not emit any byte that did not come from input. No prompt, no banner, no echo augmentation.

requirement.name: iOS Debug Entry
requirement.description: The mock TTY is reachable from inside the Debug build of the iOS app, without any SSH credential entry, by a single tap on a clearly-marked entry in the existing Hosts screen.
requirement.rule: In Debug builds, the Hosts screen displays an additional section titled "Debug TTY" with four entries: Echo Shell, Vim-Lite, Replay…, Raw Sink. In Release builds this section does not exist.
Tapping "Replay…" presents a picker listing the bundled cast fixtures by name. Selecting a fixture launches the terminal screen with the replay program preloaded with that fixture.
Tapping any Debug TTY entry pushes the existing terminal screen directly. No host, username, port, or key fields are shown, requested, or persisted.
The Debug TTY entries reuse the production terminal screen, key bar, composer, and Metal renderer unchanged. The mock TTY only replaces the SSH client.
Debug TTY labels are developer-only English strings and are not added to the localization catalogues.

requirement.name: Rust Loopback Test Coverage
requirement.description: The mock TTY's main justification for living in Rust is delivering cargo-level end-to-end regression tests over the alacritty_terminal integration.
requirement.rule: A cargo integration test pipes the mock TTY's output through alacritty_terminal's Term and asserts on the resulting grid for each echo-shell command (keys sub-mode, colors, cursor, altscreen) and for a scripted vim-lite session.
A cargo test exercises ICANON line editing, VINTR signal delivery, VEOF at line start, and raw-mode toggle round-trip.
A cargo test loads a tiny in-repo cast file and drives the tick clock with a fake time source, asserting the released byte sequence matches the cast.
These cargo tests run on every PR that touches rust-core/, in addition to the existing iOS test job.

issue.title: Proving Release builds are clean
issue.description: The "no bt_mock_tty_* in Release" guarantee depends on the build script honouring CONFIGURATION correctly and on the Cargo feature gate being airtight. An nm check on the Release xcframework slice should run in CI, and the resulting size delta between Debug and Release xcframeworks should be visible enough to catch a regression by eye.

issue.title: Cast fixtures will go stale
issue.description: Claude Code and Codex evolve quickly. The bundled cast files will eventually no longer reflect current product UI. The fixtures are intended to exercise terminal-protocol features, not to be representative of the current apps, but a periodic re-recording — and a documented "how to record one" procedure — keeps them useful.

issue.title: Output callback reentry policy is convention, not enforcement
issue.description: The Rust FFI documents that callers must not re-enter the handle from inside the output callback. A debug-assertion guard catches violations in Debug, but Swift code that accidentally re-enters in Release-with-feature builds (a developer running a custom build) would have undefined behaviour. Mitigation: the Swift wrapper serialises all FFI calls onto its own actor.
